problems: e10: pin-hole ↔ stud is not a compatible pair
notes: Booklet covers one model: 7997 Train Station. Bags 1-5 build: minifigs, hand truck and rail trolley (bag 1); platform with benches, sign gantry, ticket machine, roofs (bag 2); waiting-room building (bag 3); kiosk building (bag 4); roof, clock tower and antenna on top of the two joined buildings (bag 5).

Connectivity: the cover picture shows the minifigs standing on the platform deck, the workman on the trolley, the trolley on the track beside the platform, the station master holding the hand truck, and the station building behind the platform. These relationships are `contact` edges, not fastened joins, so the set forms one connected graph.

Legs: the printed numbers 9339 and 9341 are not real element numbers. Minifig legs are modelled as lego-970c00 with a colour prop (black or blue). The yellow '1' tile uses lego-307024 (tile 1x1 yellow).

Port handling: the validator treats each port as single-use. Many bricks and plates take several neighbours, but the catalogue gives them only one stud and one anti-stud port. Brick/plate-to-brick/plate joins therefore leave both ports null, because they are not tied to one specific stud. Named ports are kept only for pins, clips, bars, hinges, axles, wheels, track ends and some minifig parts. Where two catalogue port kinds were incompatible, the port on one side is left null.

Element IDs on pages 72-73 are small and partly illegible. Many IDs were read as best guesses, and some pieces were matched to catalogue types by shape. Part dimensions and colours are approximations.
Part counts do not match the inventory exactly. Examples: 4211407 is used 5 times against 4 listed; 4215513 is used 3 times against 4 listed.
Not placed in the graph: 301026 x2, 4211515 x4, 4211133 x6, 4211063 x3 (1 used), 4211437 x2, 362224 x4, 4210631 x1 and 4211350 x1. Their positions were not clear from the pictures.
Stickers (LEGO CITY, map, parcel label, ticket-machine screen) are printed on parts and are not separate nodes.
The two grey connecting pins shown being thrown away on page 7 (track packaging) are not modelled.

Repeated sub-assemblies (5 platform rungs, 2 bench modules, 4 deck pillars, 4 bench cap plates, roof slopes and edge plates) attach to shared external parts. The exact position of each copy along the rails or roofs is not captured.
The `joined` edges between roof panels, edge plates and pillars are plausible placements. Exactly which stud each part sits on cannot be read from the illustrations.
The two buildings (b117-b152 and b153-b192) are joined by the 2 grey pins on b122/b155. The roof assembly (b193 onward) sits on both roof plates (b147, b192).
